newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian court puts miners' leader on trial.
newsitem.headline: Romanian court puts miners' leader on trial.

text.p: The trial began on Monday of miners' leader Miron Cosma who is charged with undermining state authority during a 1991 riot which toppled the country's first post-communist government.
The court's two judges accepted a request from Cosma's lawyers to adjourn hearings to May 5 to allow them to examine the 100-page indictment and 4,500 pages of evidence.
"We need more time to examine the files in detail, because we want to establish the truth," said lawyer Viorel Dumitrescu.

A dozen lawyers representing the institutions damaged during the riots of 1991 -- the presidency, the government, parliament, the national rail and electricity companies, state television and five Bucharest hospitals -- accepted the adjournment request.

Cosma, leader of the western Jiu Valley miners' unions, was taken into police custody in January and denied bail. His lawyers claim he is a "political scapegoat". He faces a fifteen year prsison term if found guilty.
"This is a political trial. It's the first time that a case involving charges of 'undermining state authority' has been tried in our courts in fifty years," lawyer Constantin Graure told Reuters.
Cosma, 43, wearing a dark suit, waved to television cameras as police escorted him into court.

The charges of undermining state authority, breaking firearms laws, incitement to violence and threatening rail safety -- relate to his role during the 1991 riots when reformist Prime Minister Petre Roman was forced to quit.
Roman, whose Democratic party are junior partners in the new centrist ruling coalition, blamed the riots on a putsch engineered by Communists around ex-president Ion Iliescu.

The centrists, who removed the ex-communists from office in last November's elections, have vowed to bring to justice those responsible for waves of political violence in the early post-communist years.
Iliescu has denounced Cosma's arrest as "exaggerated", and has publicly denied accusations of resorting to mob rule by calling the miners to the capital to crush opposition protests
